source: XDA thread 4772596 (R0rt1z2), browser download (XDA's CDN refuses scripts)

parts.part: amonet/brom-payload/build/payload.bin and pl.bin, both built from amonet's brom-payload, which links idmetool's idmelib and carries Marco Paland's printf.c
kaeru's code in amonet/bin/cronos-kaeru.bin: every SPDX header in kaeru's source at this commit (which files this board's build pulls in is not checked); files without a header fall under its LICENSE
parts.spdx: AGPL-3.0-or-later AND MIT AND (MIT OR Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception) AND (BSD-3-Clause OR GPL-2.0-or-later) AND Unlicense AND (0BSD OR Unlicense)

parts.part: Amazon/MediaTek boot chain: amonet/bin/preloader.img, lk.bin, tz.img, tee-payload.bin, and the stock LK that cronos-kaeru.bin patches. Not in the amonet repo; the zip carries no licence or notice file
amonet/bin/twrp.img and amonet/bin/fastbrick.img: prebuilt images with no licence or notice file
amonet/bin/fastboot, fastboot32, fastboot.exe, AdbWinApi.dll, AdbWinUsbApi.dll: prebuilt Android platform tools with no licence or notice file

amonet's shell, bat and ps1 scripts, device.prop, profile.sh, profile.ps1 and META-INF's update-binary and updater-script: the repo has LICENSE.MIT and LICENSE.GPL2, but the README gives them only to modules, pl-payload, brom-payload and idmetool

notes: Reviewed 2026-10-14: update-binary and the scripts match R0rt1z2/amonet mt8163-echo-show (main.py/common.py as of 999f8d0ab5; the two commits after it only speed up bootrom-mode eMMC writes), fastbrick.sh and fastboot(32) are the same bytes as crown's, device.prop says cronos, twrp.img is the 16.1.0-20260812 omni_cronos build, and cronos-kaeru.bin is the stock kaeru install-show.py's LOGO_KAERU pins. Preloader, LK, TZ and fastbrick.img exist only in this zip. The attachment link is on the first post of the thread. The six unlock members were pinned on 2026-10-20 (GENBU-212) from this zip; they match the hash manifest the four clean cronos unlocks of 2026-10-14 ran with (those runs left no log, so they aren't evidence). Pinning them does not open unlock on cronos: unlock.py still wants a hash manifest until the evidence check exists.
